sections.title: Unit 31: Historical Trauma and Memory
body: Central and Eastern European societies have lived through borders that moved and states that disappeared. Historians and philosophers ask how such experiences shape the way a community thinks and acts. In this unit you recap forms you already know (stance adverbials, participles before a noun, contrast, purpose, scalar adverbs) and use them with the vocabulary of historical trauma and memory.

The topics are disputed, so the exercises give concepts and definitions, not verdicts. The reading is a short original text about Bibó István and his 1946 study *A kelet-európai kisállamok nyomorúsága*.
